newsitem.title: FRANCE: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON MAKES COMEBACK AT PARIS GRAND PRIX.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON MAKES COMEBACK AT PARIS GRAND PRIX.

text.p: Double Olympic champion Michael Johnson returns to the track on Wednesday for the first time since he injured a thigh muscle in a showdown with Canadian sprinter Donovan Bailey on June 1.

The American, who hurt his left leg in the 150-metre clash in Toronto, will compete over 400 metres at the Paris grand prix meeting against a field which includes compatriots Anthuan Maybank and Butch Reynolds and Britain's Olympic silver medallist Roger Black.

Bailey is also running in the French capital in the 100 metres where he is scheduled to clash with Britain's former Olympic champion Linford Christie who led the British men's team to European Cup victory in Munich at the weekend.
Johnson had orginally planned to run the 200 but changed his mind, leaving organisers to line up a top-class 400 field at the last minute.

The American, whose injury prevented him from taking part in the U.S. national championships, was forced to end his practice at the Charlety track early because of rain. But he said: "The track seems new and very fast."

Home favourite Marie-Jose Perec, women's equivalent of Johnson as holder of the Olympic 200 and 400 metres titles, will race the shorter distance after pulling out of the 400 metres hurdles saying she was not ready for the event.

Perec, who has dropped plans for a 400 hurdles and flat double at the Athens world championships in August, pulled out of France's European Cup team at the weekend because she had still not quite recovered from a stress fracture of the shin picked up during training in California.

Perec will not, however, race against compatriot Christine Arron, who in her absence won the 200 metres in the European Cup on Sunday. Arron declined a late invitation on Tuesday because she is unwell.
Another withdrawal is that of Moroccan Salah Hissou, world 10,000 metres record holder, from the 5,000 metres, in which Ethiopian Haile Gebrselassie is planning to improve his own world record.
